conventions.convention: Ordinary gauging integrates arrow-invariant U(1)-valued weights over isomorphism classes with weight 1/|Aut(x)|; gauge multiplicities are retained.
Higher gauging retains raw vertex/edge 1-gauge parameters and vertex 2-gauge transformations. Its component weight is |π2|/|π1|, rather than the ordinary cardinality of the 1-truncation.
Relative backgrounds restrict exactly to the fixed boundary field; relative arrows have identity vertex G-labels, zero edge A-labels and zero vertex 2-gauge labels on the subcomplex.
Ordinary gluing uses homotopy fibers containing boundary identifications, assumes a comparison equivalence with the homotopy pullback, and assumes invariant scalar weights factor across the pieces.
For finite ordered complexes, c(K)=|A|^(V_K−E_K)/|G|^V_K; the empty complex has one field and c=1. Gluing requires induced orders, the specified intersection and invariant factorizing scalar weights.

load_bearing.statement: An ordinary finite background field groupoid with arrow-invariant phase weight has normalized sum Σ[x] W(x)/|Aut(x)|. For the specified finite background gauge 2-groupoid and a weight constant on 1-arrows, the higher sum is Σ[x] W(x)|π2(x)|/|π1(x)|, with the stated exact relative-field and relative-arrow conventions.

For finite G, finite abelian A, an action ρ, normalized 3-cocycle β, finite ordered K and invariant scalar weight, the higher sum equals c(K) times the field-object sum. For a subcomplex L and fixed field s, the relative sum equals c(K)/c(L) times the sum over extensions of s. For K=K1∪ΣK2 with intersection Σ, induced orders and invariant factorizing weights, the relative amplitudes are boundary-gauge invariant and glue by summing their product over boundary components with weight |π2|/|π1|.

For the stated finite background groupoids and restriction functors, assuming restriction induces an equivalence with F2×^h_S F1 and the invariant phase weight factors as W2W1, the finite normalized sum satisfies Z_K(W)=Σ[s] Z2(s)Z1(s)/|Aut_S(s)|, where Zi(s) integrates over the specified homotopy fiber.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite groupoid cardinality, reciprocal automorphism weights, homotopy-fiber objects and the finiteness and representative independence of their integrals.
The ordinary gluing theorem and C2 gluing example use its triples, compatibility equation for morphisms and finiteness argument.
